claim: Baumwipfelpfad Saarschleife admission in 2026 is EUR 13 adults, EUR 11 children 6-14, free under 6, family ticket (2 adults + kids) EUR 31; reduced EUR 12.
quote: Adults: €13.00 · Reduced rate (with ID): €12.00 · Children under 6: Free entry · Children 6-14 years: €11.00 · Family ticket (2 adults + children 6-14): €31.00

claim: The Treetop Walk Saarschleife is a 1,250 m canopy walkway culminating in a 42 m observation tower, low-barrier with max 6% gradient (wheelchair/pram suitable); located at Cloef-Atrium, 66693 Mettlach-Orscholz.
quote: Tower Height: 42 metres · Walkway Length: 1,250 metres · designed to be low-barrier, with a maximum gradient of 6% and no steps

claim: Treetop Walk is open daily year-round (closed only 24 Dec); May-Oct 09:30-18:00, April until 17:00; last admission 1 hr before close; open in rain/snow, closed only for thunderstorms, hail, storms, ice.
quote: Opening hours are 09:30 to 18:00 daily, though seasonal variations apply. From May to October, the treetop walk is open from 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM. In April, it is open until 5:00 PM. Admission is possible up to 1 hour before closing time.

claim: The Cloef is a rocky viewpoint 180 m above the Saar at the apex of the loop in Mettlach-Orscholz; a 'Kleine Cloef' viewpoint sits 500 m away offering another angle; the name is Celtic for 'steep rocky valley, cliff'.
quote: The Cloef is a rocky viewing point around 180 m high above the Saar at the top of the Saar loop in the Mettlach district of Orscholz... About 500 m away is the 'Kleine Cloef'

claim: The Cloef-Atrium in Orscholz is the visitor centre next to the viewpoint, with tourist info, bistro and Regiothek for local wines/spirits; the treetop path starts directly adjacent.
quote: The Cloef-Atrium stands at one with the natural surroundings of the 'Cloef'... The modern building... serves as a conference and visitor centre and accommodates the Tourist Information Office, a bistro, and a 'Regiothek'

claim: Maria Croon Saarschleife boat from Mettlach in 2026 runs Easter-October, Tue-Sat 10:30/12:30/14:30 and Sun 11:00/14:00 (closed Mon); 90-min trip costs EUR 18 adult, EUR 10 child 4-12, EUR 40 family (2+2); bikes/dogs allowed for small fee, wheelchair accessible.
quote: Adults: €18 · Children (4-12 years): €10 · Family ticket (2 adults + 2 children): €40 · Tuesday-Saturday: 10:30, 12:30, 14:30 · Sunday: 11:00, 14:00

claim: Saar Personenschiffahrt (SPS) runs Saarschleife round trips from Mettlach starting Easter 2026; main season begins 1 May with daily round trips plus connections to Saarburg on Thursdays/Saturdays via 15:45 departure (arrives 17:30).
quote: Saar Personenschiffahrt (SPS) is starting round trips from Mettlach and Saarburg as of Easter 2026. The main season begins on May 1st... On Thursdays and Saturdays from May 1 to October 3, there is the possibility to continue to Saarburg at 15:45, arriving at 17:30 hrs.

claim: Moselsteig Stage 1 starts at the Maimuehle a few steps from Perl railway station and runs Perl - Palzem via Nennig, featuring the Dreilaenderblick three-country viewpoint where Germany, Luxembourg and France meet.
quote: The first stage of the Moselsteig Trail starts at the Maimühle (May Mill), only a few steps away from the Perl railway station... the exclusive three-country view (Dreiländerblick), where you can have a foot in two countries at the same time

claim: Moselsteig Stage 1 Perl-Palzem is 14.7 miles (~23.7 km) point-to-point, rated moderately challenging, taking on average 6 h 22 min.
quote: This is a 14.7-mile point-to-point trail that is generally considered a moderately challenging route, taking an average of 6 h 22 min to complete.

claim: The Cloef-Pfad Premiumwanderweg is a 5.3-mile (~8.5 km) loop taking on average 2.5-3 hours, an accessible day hike from the Cloef viewpoint.
quote: The Cloef Trail is a 5.3 mile loop trail that takes an average of 2.5–3 hours to complete.

claim: The Saarschleifen Tafeltour Traumschleife is a 9.9-mile (~16 km) moderate loop with 1,715 ft elevation gain, 5-5.5 hours.
quote: The Saarschleifen Tafeltour is considered a moderate hike that covers 9.9 miles, with an elevation gain of 1,715 feet, and takes about 5–5.5 hours to complete.

claim: The Mosel-Radweg runs 248 km from Perl (tri-border) to Koblenz; Stage 1 Perl-Nittel is largely flat and family-friendly on paved/traffic-separated paths, passing the Roman villa Nennig (160 sqm mosaic, open March-November) and the Pferdemosel nature reserve.
quote: the Mosel over 248 kilometers from the tri-border point in Perl to its mouth into the Rhine in Koblenz... The largest mosaic north of the Alps (160 square meters) in the Roman villa Nennig is worth a detour

claim: Saarburg waterfall cascades 20 m down the Leukbach through the medieval town centre; freely accessible from several observation platforms at the Buttermarkt.
quote: The impressive waterfall cascades 20 meters down between the narrow rows of houses in the middle of Saarburg... The waterfall at Buttermarkt is freely accessible and can be viewed from several observation platforms.

claim: Bostalsee is reachable from Perl via the Saar-Bostalsee cycle route; Losheim-to-Perl cycling distance is ~50 km, placing Bostalsee outside the 30 km radius around Perl.
quote: the cycling route from Losheim am See to Perl is approximately 50 km
